text: Adhavasana, or the state of determination, is like a seed that is the cause of a future sprout. Similarly, the determination that “this is a pot, this is a cloth,” and so on, is characterized as a cognition (buddhi). This cognition is eightfold. Due to the difference in its nature, it is of three types: sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic. The sattvic form of cognition is fourfold: dharma (righteousness), jnana (knowledge), vairagya (dispassion), and aishvarya (sovereignty). Dharma is characterized by compassion, charity, restraint, and observance. The restraints (yamas) and observances (niyamas) are as stated by Patanjali: the yamas are non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness; the niyamas are purity, contentment, austerity, self-study, and surrender to the Lord.
